'''Mark D. Bertness''' (born July 13, 1949) is an American [[ecology|ecologist]], known for his work on the [[community ecology|community assembly]] of marine shoreline communities.<ref name="Bertness">Bertness, M.D. 2006. Atlantic Shoreline Ecology: A Natural History. Princeton University Press</ref>

Among his important work are the Stress Gradient Hypothesis (Bertness and [[Ragan Callaway|Callaway]] 1994<ref name="planta">{{cite web|url=http://www.planta.cn/forum/files_planta/positive_interactions_in_communities_147.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141119185916/http://www.planta.cn/forum/files_planta/positive_interactions_in_communities_147.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 November 2014|title=Positive interactions in communities|publisher=Planta.cn|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref>) that predicts that positive species interactions are more important in biologically and physically stressful habitats than in biologically and physically benign habitats, his experimental research in a variety of marine [[Intertidal ecology|intertidal communities]] elucidating the roles of biotic interaction across intertidal gradients<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=t0gaAAAAIBAJ&sjid=YiYEAAAAIBAJ&dq=mark-bertness&pg=6792%2C5647184|title=The Times-News - Google News Archive Search|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=t0gaAAAAIBAJ&sjid=YiYEAAAAIBAJ&dq=mark-bertness&pg=6590%2C5647186|title=The Times-News - Google News Archive Search|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref> (Bertness and Hacker 1994,<ref name="userwww.sfsu">{{cite web|url=http://userwww.sfsu.edu/parker/bio529/pdfs/BertnessHPosInt.pdf|title=Positive Stress ... Among Marsh Plants|publisher=Sfsu.edu|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref> Bertness et al. 1999,<ref name="Doi">{{cite journal| title = Testing the Relative Contribution of Positive and Negative Interactions in Rocky Intertidal Communities| last1 = Bertness | first1 = M. D.| last2 = Leonard | first2 = G. H.| last3 = Levine | first3 = J. M.| journal = Ecology| last4 = Schmidt | first4 = P. R.| last5 = Ingraham | first5 = A. O.| year = 1999| pages = 2711–2726| volume = 80| issue = 8| publisher = Ecological Society of America| issn = 0012-9658| doi = 10.1890/0012-9658(1999)080[2711:TTRCOP]2.0.CO;2}}</ref> Bertness 1999<ref name="Doi_a">{{cite journal| doi = 10.2307/1938431| title = Intraspecific Competition and Facilitation in a Northern Acorn Barnacle Population | first1 = M. D.| last1 = Bertness| journal = Ecology| volume = 70| issue = 1| year = 1989| pages = 257–268| publisher = Ecological Society of America| jstor = 1938431| bibcode = 1989Ecol...70..257B }}</ref>), his pioneering of experimental community ecology in [[salt marsh]] ecosystems<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.boston.com/lifestyle/green/greenblog/2009/08/some_waterloving_plants_may_en.html |accessdate=October 30, 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018092110/http://www.boston.com/lifestyle/green/greenblog/2009/08/some_waterloving_plants_may_en.html |archivedate=October 18, 2012 |title=Some water-loving plants may be out of a home as temperatures rise - the Green Blog - A Boston Globe blog on living Green in Boston }}</ref><ref name="Doi_b">{{cite journal| doi = 10.2307/1938909| title = Zonation of Spartina Patens and Spartina Alterniflora in New England Salt Marsh | first1 = M. D. | last1 = Bertness| journal = Ecology| volume = 72| issue = 1| year = 1991| pages = 138–148| publisher = Ecological Society of America| jstor = 1938909| bibcode = 1991Ecol...72..138B }}</ref> and his work on [[apex predator]] depletion causing die-offs in salt marshes due to the release of herbivores from predator control <ref>{{cite news|url=http://archive.boston.com/news/science/articles/2007/11/19/cape_salt_marsh_decline_linked_to_native_crab/|title=Cape salt marsh decline linked to native crab|newspaper=Boston.com|access-date=13 November 2014|date=2007-11-19|last1=Lewis|first1=Richard C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ens-newswire.com/ens/aug2002/2002-08-07-06.asp|title=Blue Crab Decline May Herald Salt Marsh Loss|publisher=Ens-newswire.com|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite Herrmann|first4 = Nicholas C.|last5 = Angelini|first5 = Christine| bibcode=2012Ecol...93.1402A }}</ref>

Bertness is the Professor Emeritus of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology and former chair of the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at [[Brown University]].<ref name="brown">{{cite web|url=https://www.brown.edu/Departments/EEB/|title=Welcome!|publisher=Brown.edu|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref> He has had visiting distinguished appointments at [[Groningen University]], the Netherlands,<ref name="rug">{{cite web|url=http://www.rug.nl/corporate/index?lang=en|title=Top 100 University - Rijksuniversiteit Groningen|publisher=Rug.nl|accessdate=13 November 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107020632/http://www.rug.nl/corporate/index?lang=en|archivedate=7 November 2012}}</ref> the Catholic University of Santiago, Chile<ref name="uc">{{cite web|url=http://www.uc.cl/|title=Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile|publisher=Uc.cl|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref> and the [[University of Sassari]], Sardinia, Italy.<ref name="uniss">{{cite web|url=http://www.uniss.it/php/home.php|title=Uniss - Homepage|publisher=Uniss.it|accessdate=13 November 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141018102723/http://www.uniss.it/php/home.php|archivedate=18 October 2014}}</ref>

In 2002 Bertness has been designated an ISI and Web of Science [[Highly Cited Researcher]] in Environmental Science;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://researchanalytics.thomsonreuters.com/highlycited/names/b/ |accessdate=October 30, 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130502003936/http://researchanalytics.thomsonreuters.com/highlycited/names/b/ |archivedate=May 2, 2013 |title=InCites }}</ref> this indicates that Dr. Bertness was among the 250 most-cited researchers in Environmental Science during a certain period of time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://researchanalytics.thomsonreuters.com/highlycited/directory/ |accessdate=October 30, 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130127110642/http://researchanalytics.thomsonreuters.com/highlycited/directory/ |archivedate=January 27, 2013 |title=InCites }}</ref> In 2009, Bertness was recognized as a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2008-12/bu-fbf121808.php|title=5 Brown faculty elected to world's largest scientific body|date=18 December 2008|publisher=Eurekalert.org|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref> this fellowship is a recognition of an individual's meritorious efforts to advance science or its applications.<ref name="aaas">{{cite web|url=http://www.aaas.org/aboutaaas/fellows/|title=General Process|publisher=Aaas.org|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref> Bertness is also a trustee of the [[Marine Biological Association of the United Kingdom]].<ref name="mba">{{cite web|url=http://www.mba.ac.uk/|title=Marine Biological Association of the UK|author=Steve Pewter|publisher=Mba.ac.uk|accessdate=13 November 2014}}</ref>
